Android TV box buyer's guide

A short, practical checklist for choosing a set-top box by hardware specs — not by IPTV promises. Shop published models at TV boxes.

Last updated: September 23, 2026

On this pageWhat it isWho it is forSpec checklistLegal hardware positioningStarting picksFAQ

What is an Android TV box?

An Android TV box is a small computer designed for your television. It outputs video over HDMI, connects to Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and runs an Android-based system so you can install apps from official stores or sideload only what you are licensed to use.

Think of it as hardware: the box does not replace a paid streaming subscription. You bring your own accounts.

Who should buy one?

  • Households that want a dedicated device for the living-room TV
  • Travelers or renters who need a compact HDMI stick/box for hotels or temporary setups
  • Buyers comparing chipsets and memory instead of vague “channel pack” marketing

Spec checklist before you pay

  • Chipset / CPU — drives decode smoothness and app responsiveness
  • OS version — listed on each CRTLU product page (for example Android 11 or 14)
  • RAM + storage — more RAM helps multitasking; more storage holds more apps
  • Wi-Fi / Ethernet — dual-band or Wi-Fi 6 plus wired LAN when available
  • HDMI — confirm 4K/HDR expectations match your TV
  • Power plug — choose UK / EU / US at checkout when a wall adapter is included

How this differs from IPTV-branded boxes

Search terms like UBOX, UNBLOCK, or EVPAD often appear when shoppers look for “TV boxes with channels.” CRTLU Digital does not sell piracy packages or lifetime unofficial TV services. We sell Android TV / streaming hardware so you can use Netflix, YouTube, and other official apps with accounts you own.

Guide FAQ

What is an Android TV box?

An Android TV box is a compact set-top computer that connects to a TV over HDMI. You install official apps, sign in with your own accounts, and play media your subscriptions allow.

Is a CRTLU Digital TV box the same as an IPTV brand box?

No. CRTLU Digital sells hardware for official apps and customer-owned subscriptions. We do not include preloaded paid IPTV packages or unauthorized channel services.

Which configuration should beginners buy?

Start with a clear chipset and Wi-Fi listing on the product page. For everyday apps, prefer at least 4GB RAM when budget allows; 2GB + 16GB is an entry option for lighter use.
